newsitem.title: USA: Black Rock Golf secures credit line.
newsitem.headline: Black Rock Golf secures credit line.

text.p: Black Rock Golf Corp said on Friday it had secured a $800,000 revolving line of credit through Norwest Business Credit Inc, a susidiary of Norwest Bank.

Jack Rule, the company's chief executive said in a statement that the loan would help the company "to expand the scope of operations and in purchasing from its manufacturers the needed gold club components to support increasing sales."
Black Rock also reported 1996 earnings Friday, showing a net loss of $1.8 million, or 70 cents per share.
The company attributed the net loss to a shift in consumer demand from stainless steel to titanium clubs, and to late delivery from vendors of inventory of new product offerings.

The company also said its net loss reflected a USGA nonconforming letter issued on March 7, 1997. The USGA ruling was reversed on April 11, but the company recorded additional losses due to returned and modified clubs and legal fees, the company said.
Because the modifications were to clubs issued in 1995 and 1996, the costs were recorded retroactively, said Gerald Fick, the company's chief financial officer.
Black Rock designs and markets extra length golf clubs.
